description: Galaxy Coders is a multidisciplinary team combining coding, AI, software, hardware, data analysis, web development, design, and multimedia. We aim to transform space science and NASA data into innovative, interactive, and engaging solutions through creativity, teamwork, and technology.
summary:
Terra Nova is a unique interactive website, which was developed as a link between Earth and deep space with the help of geological and environmental analogues of the Moon and Mars.

What did we do?: We have developed an easy-to-use web-site that includes two kinds of visualization – 3D Globe and 2D Map (Satellite and Street view). This web-site allows one to explore analogues of the Earth to Mars and Earth to Moon sites – Atacama desert, Wadi Rum, Mars Desert Research Station (MDRS) and much more. In addition to that all these sites have geographic and scientific data.

Why does it help to solve the problem? Before sending astronauts and/or robots to other planets space agencies such as NASA use earth analogues to test and prepare for this mission. Data offered by Terra Nova platform is very helpful from scientific and motivating perspective as it shows how close we are to the Moon and Mars.
details:
How It Works:

Terra Nova is a user-friendly interactive website connecting Earth exploration to planetary science by creating analog maps between terrestrial sites and the lunar and Martian surfaces. This project offers the ability to easily toggle between an interactive 3D Globe and 2D Map (including Satellite and Street views) and explore different analog Earth-Mars and Earth-Moon sites, such as the Atacama Desert, Wadi Rum, McMurdo Dry Valleys, and Mars Desert Research Station (MDRS). Simply click on any given site to access its geographic coordinates, images, and scientific information explaining why this particular place serves as an analog to extraterrestrial environment.

Benefits and Intended Effect:

As it was already mentioned, NASA makes use of terrestrial analog sites extensively to develop rovers and train astronauts before sending missions into space. The purpose of our project is to visualize the vast information about planetary geology in order to give students, researchers, and enthusiasts insight into how learning about our planet will allow us to explore the Moon and Mars.

Tools and Technologies:

Front End: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript.

Mapping and visualization tools: Interactive 3D Globe and 2D web mapping libraries (with Satellite and Street map layers).

Data and hosting: Data about scientific analog sites compiled from NASA resources and sources on planetary research hosted publicly on GitHub Pages.

Creativity and Key Considerations:

Our team paid much attention to usability and visual communication by implementing a unique combination of dual 3D/2D interface with easy-to-use side-by-side comparison menus in order to make anyone able to compare Earth's extreme environment with the Moon and Mars surfaces.
